emma: FYI escalation from Acme — large batch job hitting intermittent 500s on /v1/embeddings since 2026-03-16T08:12Z. They also saw occasional 401 before the 500s. Need tiny repro and request IDs.
acme_support: Hey team — posting the simple curl we use in the worker. Batch is 100 items normally. We see 401 once in a while then later 500s.
acme_support: ```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live:ACME\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":["a","b",.../*100 items*/]}' \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
raj: Can you capture full response headers + body (use -i) and paste any X-Request-ID/X-Trace-ID? Also which SDK/lang?
acme_support: Node 18 using an internal wrapper over the JS SDK. Short log snippet when it fails: `ERROR embeddings request failed status=500 request_id=rcw-4f7c2d`
emma: Good — that rcw ID is helpful. @kevin can you take lead? We need: 1) any rcw-* ids from failing attempts, 2) very small repros (curl/pysnippet/js/go) to reproduce batch=1 vs batch=100, 3) whether tokens rotate during the job.
kevin: Will do. Quick checklist for customer: include -i for headers, run with batch size 1 and 100, collect request ids, note UTC time window.
maria: Also ask them to run the JS SDK with DEBUG=redwood:* to show trace ids and request headers.
raj: Minimal snippets to ask them to run — keep single-file and tiny.
raj: ```js
// repro.js
import Redwood from '@redwoodai/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
(async()=>{
  const r = await client.embeddings.create({ model:'text-embedding-3-small', input:['hello'] });
  console.log('status', r.status);
  console.log('headers', r.headers);
  console.log('body', await r.json());
})();
```
raj: ```py
# repro.py
import os
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='text-embedding-3-small', input=['hello'])
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers)
print(resp.json())
```
raj: ```go
// repro.go
package main
import (
  "context"
  "fmt"
  "log"
  "os"

  "github.com/redwoodai/redwood-go"
)
func main(){
  client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
  resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(context.Background(), redwood.EmbeddingParams{Model:"text-embedding-3-small", Input:[]string{"hello"}})
  if err!=nil{ log.Fatal(err) }
  fmt.Println(resp.Status)
  fmt.Println(resp.Headers)
}
```
emma: Ask them to try each with single item and with ~100 items. Also request they mask tokens when pasting.
acme_support: Running now. Quick Q: how to best script split into smaller batches for curl?
kevin: Simple python one-liner will chunk JSON and POST each chunk. Works fine.

maria: I pulled logs for rcw-4f7c2d — staging repro shows a kernel OOM on a GPU when sequence lengths vary across the batch. There's KV cache pressure and an allocation spike. Posting snippet to eng-runtime in a bit.
raj: As immediate mitigation ask them to reduce batch size to 16 or split client-side. Also consider enabling prefix caching or padding to uniform length.
acme_support: We can do that. We'll test 16 and 32 and report back. Also we'll enable DEBUG env to capture SDK trace ids.
kevin: I'll open INF ticket linking rcw-4f7c2d and include staging traces. If this lines up with the recent batching kernel change we can roll that back quickly.
